$Comment: What a player sees and hears when one tier of a gear set comes on or goes off for them: the
recompute after an equip change found the tier's minimums newly met, or newly unmet. It fires
only for a real change; logging in wearing a full set is a hydrate and says nothing.
This is the library's own neutral default, so a bare server gets a notice out of the box. A
mod that ships a file with this same name in its own pack replaces it (a pack that lists this
library as a dependency loads after it), and a server owner can do the same from the owner
layer. Override the whole file rather than editing this one.
The moment carries 'set' (the set id, also under 'source' so a merging notice keeps one line
per set), 'name' (what the set is called, already in the reader's language), 'pieces' (how
many distinct members the player has on), 'total' (how many the set has), 'desc' (the tier's
own line, in the reader's language; absent when the tier authors no Text) and 'active' (true
when the tier came on, false when it went off). 'player' is always the name of who wears it.
Key is a line from a .lang file; Args names which of those values fill its blanks, in order.
Sound is any SoundEvent id, played at the player's own position. Delete either group in your
override to drop that half; add a Broadcast group to tell the whole server. Tone colours the
whole notification: gold Reward for a bonus coming on, plain Info for one going off, which is
what the Variants entry below says for the 'active: false' case.
